subject: music
topicDisplay: Areas Of Inquiry Music For Sociocultural And Political Expression
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A 'hook' in popular music is best described as...?
options: The final cadence of the song
A device for tuning the guitar
A modulation to the relative minor
A short, catchy musical idea designed to grab the listener and stick in the memory
questions.explain: A hook is a memorable, catchy idea engineered to capture and hold the listener's attention.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is which?
questions.explain: C up to G spans seven semitones, a perfect fifth.

questions.q: In music production, 'multitracking' refers to...?
options: Recording different parts onto separate tracks so they can be balanced and edited independently
Compressing a stereo mix into mono
Playing many instruments live in one take with no overdubs
questions.explain: Multitracking records parts on separate tracks, allowing independent editing and mixing.

questions.q: In jazz harmony, 'comping' refers to...?
options: Compressing the dynamic range in the mix
Counting the band in before a number
Composing a fully notated arrangement in advance
A pianist or guitarist playing improvised, syncopated chordal accompaniment behind a soloist
questions.explain: Comping is the improvised, rhythmic chordal accompaniment provided by piano or guitar behind a soloist.

questions.q: The whole-tone scale, favoured by Debussy, divides the octave into how many equal steps?
questions.explain: The whole-tone scale consists of six pitches a whole tone apart, lacking semitones and a clear tonic.

questions.q: In an Indian classical ensemble, which pairing of instruments is most typical?
questions.explain: The sitar plays the melody while the tabla provides the rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: A Lied is which type of composition?
options: A German art song for voice and piano
questions.explain: The Lied is a German Romantic art song, typically for solo voice and piano.

questions.q: A diminished seventh chord is built from which stacked intervals?
options: A major third and two minor thirds
questions.explain: The diminished seventh chord consists of three stacked minor thirds, dividing the octave symmetrically.

questions.q: In the genre of the stage musical, an 'I want' song typically functions to...?
options: Resolve the plot in the finale
Express a principal character's central desire or goal early in the show
questions.explain: The 'I want' song establishes the protagonist's driving desire, usually near the start of a musical.

questions.q: In African drumming traditions, the West African 'djembe' is...?
options: A set of tuned metal gongs
questions.explain: The djembe is a goblet-shaped West African hand drum capable of a wide range of tones.

questions.q: A German augmented sixth chord contains which intervals above the bass?
options: Major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth
Major third and augmented sixth only
Major third, augmented fourth and augmented sixth
questions.explain: The German sixth comprises a major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth above the bass note.

questions.q: Handel's 'Messiah' belongs to which genre?
questions.explain: 'Messiah' is an English oratorio, a large sacred work for soloists, chorus and orchestra without staging.

questions.q: In music production, 'panning' controls...?
options: The overall loudness of the master
The amount of reverb on a track
The placement of a sound within the stereo field (left to right)
questions.explain: Panning positions a sound across the stereo image from left to right.

questions.q: In the typical structure of a North Indian raga performance, the opening section is the 'alap', which is characterised by...?
options: A fast, fixed composition with drumming
A slow, free, unmetred exploration of the raga without tabla
questions.explain: The alap is the slow, unmetred opening that introduces the raga's notes, performed without the tabla.

questions.q: Which woodwind instrument was a notable addition to the orchestra during the Classical-to-Romantic expansion?
questions.explain: The clarinet became a standard orchestral instrument from the late Classical period onward.

questions.q: Basso continuo is most strongly associated with which period of music?
questions.explain: Basso continuo, a continuous bass with realised harmony, is a defining feature of Baroque music.

questions.q: 'Scat singing' in jazz is...?
options: Singing only the written lyrics with no variation
Singing in strict unison with the bass line
Vocal improvisation using nonsense syllables to imitate an instrument
questions.explain: Scat singing improvises wordless, nonsense syllables, treating the voice like an improvising instrument.

questions.q: The effect known as 'delay' produces which result?
options: A widening of the stereo field by phase inversion
One or more distinct repeats (echoes) of the original signal
A panning of sound between left and right speakers
questions.explain: Delay creates discrete repeats, or echoes, of the original sound.

questions.q: The standard Classical string quartet comprises which instruments?
options: Violin, viola, cello and double bass
questions.explain: A string quartet is scored for two violins, one viola and one cello.

questions.q: In strict four-part writing, which is a forbidden parallel motion?
questions.explain: Consecutive (parallel) perfect fifths and octaves are prohibited in traditional voice-leading.

questions.q: Which composer is often called the 'father of the symphony' and the 'father of the string quartet'?
questions.explain: Haydn's extensive output shaped both the Classical symphony and the string quartet.

questions.q: In the standard jazz turnaround, a ii-V-I progression in the key of C major uses which three chords in order?
questions.explain: In C major the supertonic seventh is Dm7, the dominant seventh is G7 and the tonic is Cmaj7.

questions.q: Vivaldi's 'The Four Seasons' is an example of which Baroque genre?
questions.explain: 'The Four Seasons' consists of four solo violin concertos, a leading Baroque solo-concerto example.

questions.q: Beethoven's symphonies are generally seen as bridging which two stylistic periods?
questions.explain: Beethoven extended Classical forms toward Romantic expression, bridging the two eras.

questions.q: Chopin's output is dominated by works for which instrument?
questions.explain: Chopin wrote almost exclusively for solo piano, including nocturnes, mazurkas and ballades.

questions.q: Serialism, as developed by Schoenberg, organises pitches using which device?
questions.explain: Schoenberg's twelve-tone (serial) method orders all twelve chromatic pitches into a tone row that governs the music.

questions.q: Which jazz style, emerging in the 1940s, is defined by fast tempos, complex chord substitutions and virtuosic improvisation, associated with Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie?
questions.explain: Bebop is the fast, harmonically complex and virtuosic jazz style pioneered by Parker and Gillespie.

questions.q: Wagner's term for a recurring musical theme associated with a character or idea is which?
questions.explain: Wagner used leitmotifs, short recurring themes representing characters, objects or ideas in his music dramas.

questions.q: The 'blue notes' that give the blues scale its characteristic flavour are most typically the flattened third, flattened fifth and flattened...?
questions.explain: The blues scale lowers the third, fifth and seventh degrees, producing the expressive 'blue' inflections.

questions.q: When 'arranging' an existing melody for a new ensemble, a composer is chiefly concerned with...?
options: Transposing it down exactly one semitone only
Re-scoring and adapting existing material for different forces while retaining its essence
Inventing an entirely new melody unrelated to the original
questions.explain: Arranging adapts and re-scores existing material for different forces while preserving its identity.
